central_assessment: A derivational/stative/participial domain centered on *-ame now has explicit continuity across Proto-Tarahumara reconstruction, a seventeenth-century gamek attestation, Steffel's eighteenth-century -ga + -(a)me + -ke chains, and modern -ga + -me/-ame constructions. The strongest working model for color morphology is retention plus later semantic/analogical specialization, not a universal mechanical -ameke > -ami rule.

historical_layers.evidence: *-ame adjectivalizer/nominalizer/participial; late PT stative constructions contain *-ame.
Guadalaxara Pedro norugamek provides a pre-Steffel stative gamek chain.
Merrill explicitly segments stative -ga~-ja + participial -(a)me + final -ke in chains such as -rúgameke; Steffel reports frequent omission of final -ke.
Participial -ame/-me, adjective/state -ga-me, color forms in -ka/-ga/-cha + -me, and productive color-state -ga are documented independently.

historical_participial_bridge: čókameke ~ čókame -> modern chó-ka-me / chó-ka-mi / chó-ko-m
rosákameke ~ rosákame -> modern rosá-ka-me / rosá-ka-mi / rosá-ko-m
color_morphology.historical_na_bridge: tsestá-na 'is red' is explicitly segmented historically and compared to modern sitá-na 'be/become red'; modern -na is productive throughout the color paradigm.
color_morphology.historical_ga_evidence: Steffel/Merrill explicitly document stative -ga~-ja with -(a)meke. Merrill proposes that -gameke in schiógameke could be a variant of the -cameke ending of the other basic colors because g/c alternate historically.
color_morphology.modern_ga_evidence: The 1997 multivariety Compendio explicitly has -ga-me outside and inside colors and productive color-state -ga; it groups -ka/-ga/-cha as high/intense color modifiers before participial -me.

hypothesis_ranking.label: Retention plus specialization
hypothesis_ranking.assessment: An inherited stative -ga + participial -ame(+ke) architecture persisted, while the color subsystem regularized or specialized dialectal -ka/-ga forms and contrasted them with -na.

hypothesis_ranking.label: Retention without reconstructed specialization chronology
hypothesis_ranking.assessment: Historical -cameke/-gameke broadly continues old stative/participial morphology, but the modern semantic organization cannot yet be dated.

hypothesis_ranking.label: Pure late reanalysis
hypothesis_ranking.assessment: Possible locally, but less economical as a global explanation because explicit -ga+ame architecture exists both historically and modernly.

claims_supported: The *-ame domain is reconstructible before the documentary period.
Stative ga+ame-like architecture predates Steffel and remains visible in modern varieties.
Steffel's -ameke can contain independently segmentable participial -(a)me plus final -ke; final -ke was often omitted.
Historical and modern color systems contain at least two independent morphological bridges: -kameke~-kame to -ka-me and -na to -na.
Modern color morphology itself preserves -ga-me and productive -ga, so modern -ka-me need not be explained solely through late reanalysis.
claims_not_supported: Automatic identity of every historical color c/k with stative -ga or modern -ka.
A single automatic k~g alternation in all Rarámuri environments.
A securely dated innovation point for the modern semantic contrast -ka/-ga versus -na.

priority_candidates.interpretation: Grade A marks evidential architecture, not final cognation.

next_phase: Construct a controlled historical-modern k~g series in comparable morphophonological environments.
Date the emergence/specialization of the modern color opposition -ka/-ga versus -na using earlier twentieth-century descriptions where accessible.
Seek direct access to the unpublished Steffel 1799 grammar or a scholarly transcription.
epistemic_rule: System-level continuity and lexeme-level segmentation are separate claims and must carry separate confidence values.
